common_name: Southwestern Desert Riparian Fly (ebony/tan Cis-Regulatory Carotenoid Yellow Body)

chronoseries.note: Catalog chronoseries neighbors at 0 Ma, not a claim of direct anagenesis. Mojavensis is a cactophilic repleta-group fly; orena is a melanogaster-subgroup cloud-forest endemic. The comparison is the reconstructed reaction-rate scale at this 1.9 µm question.

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila novamexicana (1.9 µm, detail scale)

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg (1979): f = a - u + u^2 v, g = b - u^2 v
equations.pde: dt u = gamma f + Du lap u; dt v = gamma g + Dv lap v
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = gamma (Dv fu + Du gv) / (2 Du Dv)
equations.boundary_conditions: periodic 5-point Laplacian on a square abdominal-cuticle patch

parameters.note: gamma triple is specific to slot 3195 at 1.9 µm. It is not the alpha_scale used by the 96 µm mojavensis slot (1.33) or the 89 µm orena slot (1.78).

empirical_claims: Turing (1952) derived a critical wavenumber from the linearized reaction-diffusion dispersion relation.
Schnakenberg (1979) introduced the trimolecular activator-substrate kinetics used here.
Murray (1981) showed that a reaction-rate scale gamma shortens the chemical wavelength as gamma^{-1/2}.

Wittkopp et al. (2009, Science 326:540-544) showed that the light abdominal cuticle of D. novamexicana relative to dark D. americana is caused in large part by derived cis-regulatory alleles of ebony and tan.
Lamb et al. (2020) showed that ebony contributes to pigmentation divergence, and to cuticular hydrocarbons, between D. americana and D. novamexicana.
The 1.901 µm figure is this slot's assigned subcellular detail scale. It is not a spacing Wittkopp or Lamb measured on a micrograph.
